title: Frontend: scaffold Vite + React + TypeScript + MUI project
description: Foundational task: create the frontend/ project from scratch (currently not yet scaffolded, per CLAUDE.md's repo layout). Nothing else in the frontend-* task family can start before this lands. Establishes the toolchain, MUI theme, TanStack Query provider, routing shell, and the test/Storybook harness — no feature UI yet.

checklist.step: Scaffold frontend/ with Vite + React + TypeScript (strict mode on in tsconfig.json).

Install and configure MUI (@mui/material, @mui/icons-material, @emotion/react, @emotion/styled) with a theme.ts under src/theme/ — define a palette including semantic colors for BUY/SELL/HOLD signals and risk-rule-breach warnings, per Frontend.md.
Install and configure @tanstack/react-query: QueryClientProvider wired in main.tsx/App.tsx with sane defaults (retry, staleTime) documented inline.
Install react-router-dom and set up the route table in App.tsx (routes can point at placeholder pages until frontend-app-shell-navigation and the page tasks land).
Set up ESLint + Prettier (or the project's preferred lint/format pair) with npm scripts (lint, format).

Set up the test harness: vitest + @testing-library/react + msw, matching docs/architecture/Testing.md's coverage config exactly (v8 provider, 90% lines/branches/functions/statements thresholds) in vite.config.ts.
Set up Storybook (storybook + @storybook/react-vite, plus an accessibility addon) with .storybook/main.ts and preview.ts wired to the MUI theme.
Add package.json scripts: dev, build, test, test:coverage, storybook, build-storybook.
Update CLAUDE.md's repo layout line for frontend/ to remove '(not yet scaffolded)' and briefly describe the stack.

Confirm `npm run test:coverage`, `npm run build`, and `npm run build-storybook` all succeed on the empty scaffold (no coverage gate failure expected yet since there's no application code to cover below the threshold — document how the coverage gate is meant to behave once features land, per Testing.md).

decisions.decision: Used `npm create vite@latest frontend -- --template react-ts` and let npm resolve current latest versions for every package rather than hand-pinning older versions: React 19.2.8, MUI 9.4.0, Vite 8.3.0, TypeScript ~6.0.2, ESLint 10.10.0 (flat config), vitest 5.0.1 / @vitest/coverage-v8 5.0.1, Storybook 10.6.0.
decisions.rationale: No architecture doc pins exact versions, only package names (Frontend.md §6). Taking whatever npm resolves as current keeps the scaffold on a toolchain that will actually receive support/fixes for the ~9 dependent frontend-* tasks still to come, rather than deliberately starting behind. Verified the whole chain (build, lint, vitest+coverage, storybook build) actually works together before treating this as settled, rather than assuming compatibility from version numbers alone.

decisions.decision: Chose ESLint + Prettier over the create-vite default (oxlint) for lint/format.
decisions.rationale: The checklist named 'ESLint + Prettier (or the project's preferred lint/format pair)' as the primary option. ESLint's plugin ecosystem (eslint-plugin-react-hooks, eslint-plugin-storybook, typescript-eslint) is what the later frontend-* tasks and Storybook integration expect; oxlint's plugin surface for this project's needs (react-hooks rules-of-hooks, storybook story linting) is thinner. Removed the generated .oxlintrc.json and its dependency.

decisions.decision: Ran `storybook init` but pruned its auto-added @storybook/addon-vitest, @chromatic-com/storybook, and @storybook/addon-mcp, keeping only @storybook/addon-a11y (the task's required accessibility addon) and @storybook/addon-docs.
decisions.rationale: addon-vitest wires a Playwright-backed browser test project into vite.config.ts and downloads Chromium binaries (with a printed warning about missing system deps) — a heavy, out-of-scope addition the checklist didn't ask for, and one that would have made vite.config.ts's coverage config a multi-project setup rather than matching Testing.md's example 'exactly' as required. Chromatic (cloud visual-review SaaS) and the MCP addon are unrelated to any checklist item. All three can be added later in a task that actually wants them, with review of the tradeoff at that point.

decisions.decision: Kept .storybook/preview.tsx as a .tsx file rather than .ts, even though the checklist says 'preview.ts'.
decisions.rationale: The MUI ThemeProvider decorator that wires every story to src/theme/theme.ts (required by the same checklist line) returns JSX, which needs a .tsx extension to compile under this project's TypeScript/Vite config. Read 'preview.ts' as shorthand for 'the preview config file', not a literal ban on JSX in it — this is Storybook's own documented convention for a themed decorator.

decisions.decision: Added a minimal but real baseline test suite (src/App.test.tsx covering the route table, src/theme/theme.test.ts covering the semantic palette) instead of leaving the scaffold with zero tests.
decisions.rationale: vitest exits non-zero ('No test files found') when no test file exists, which would make `npm run test:coverage` fail — directly contradicting the checklist's 'confirm test:coverage ... succeed on the empty scaffold' requirement. Testing the route table and theme palette is legitimate coverage of the actual scaffold code (App.tsx, pages/*, theme.ts) rather than a throwaway assertion, and reaches 100% on all four coverage dimensions without pulling forward any frontend-* feature work.

decisions.decision: Fixed the pr-reviewer blocking finding by adding `coverage.include: ['src/**/*.{ts,tsx}']` to vite.config.ts rather than `coverage.all: true` as the review comment suggested.
decisions.rationale: Checked the installed vitest 5.0.1 / @vitest/coverage-v8 5.0.1 type definitions (node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/plugin.d.CN87HSxv.d.ts, interface CoverageOptions) directly rather than assuming the option name: there is no `all` field in this version's CoverageOptions at all, only `include`/`exclude`, and `include`'s own doc comment says 'By default only files covered by tests are included' — i.e. setting `include` is this version's mechanism for switching from tested-files-only to all-matching-files, replacing the older `coverage.all` boolean from earlier vitest majors. Verified empirically the same way the reviewer did: added a throwaway src/scratch-untested.ts with an untested if/else branch, reran `npm run test:coverage` — it now appeared in the report and dragged coverage from 100% to 62.5%, correctly failing the 90% threshold gate (previously the run stayed unchanged at 100% with the file invisible). Removed the throwaway file and confirmed `npm run test:coverage` passes cleanly again at 100% on all four dimensions.

comments.summary: Re-review of the fix for the previously blocking coverage-gap finding. task-worker added `coverage.include: ['src/**/*.{ts,tsx}']` to frontend/vite.config.ts, citing the installed vitest 5.0.1 `CoverageOptions` type definitions as having no `all` field, only `include`/`exclude`. Independently confirmed this by reading node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/plugin.d.CN87HSxv.d.ts myself (interface CoverageOptions has no `all` member; `include`'s doc comment reads 'By default only files covered by tests are included'). Reproduced the original empirical test myself from scratch: added a throwaway frontend/src/scratch-untested.ts with an untested if/else branch, ran `npm run test:coverage` — it now appeared in the report and coverage correctly dropped to 62.5%/0% branches, failing the 90% threshold with a non-zero exit (ERROR: Coverage for lines/functions/statements/branches does not meet global threshold). Removed the throwaway file and reran: back to a clean 100% on all four dimensions. The fix is empirically sound, not just plausible from the type defs. Not blocking.

docs/architecture/Testing.md's frontend coverage example (the vite.config.ts code block under §Frontend) still omits `include`, so the documented source of truth — which the original frontend-scaffold checklist named as the config vite.config.ts must match — doesn't show the mechanism that makes the 90% gate actually count untested files, unlike the backend example's `source = ["app"]` which already documents the equivalent behavior. A future task copying this doc's snippet verbatim would reintroduce the exact bug just fixed. Non-blocking (the shipped vite.config.ts itself is correct); filed as a follow-up on frontend-scaffold-followups. Raised by the code-review skill's pass over this fix commit.

src/theme/theme.ts's typography.fontFamily lists "Inter" first, but the font is never actually loaded anywhere (no <link> in index.html, no @fontsource/inter or Google Fonts import, no @font-face) — every page silently falls through to the next stack entry (system font) instead of Inter. Cosmetic, non-blocking; tracked in frontend-scaffold-followups (carried over from the prior review round, unchanged by this fix).

review.notes: Re-review of PR #61 after task-worker's fix commit (4bb0676) for the previously blocking coverage include/all gap. Verified the fix soundly rather than trusting the claim: read the installed vitest 5.0.1 CoverageOptions type definitions myself to confirm no `all` field exists and `include` is the documented replacement, then independently reproduced the empirical before/after test (throwaway untested file with an untested branch correctly drags coverage down and fails the gate; removing it restores a clean 100% pass). Re-ran the full verification pass: npm run test:coverage, npm run lint, npm run format:check, npm run build, and npm run build-storybook all pass on the fixed branch; backend suite re-run as a regression check (472 passed, 99.84% coverage, unaffected — this PR touches no backend code). Ran the code-review skill against the fix commit's diff (frontend/vite.config.ts + task-board bookkeeping); it independently traced vitest's config-resolution code to confirm test files/setup files stay excluded from coverage even with the new `include`, and surfaced one new non-blocking finding (Testing.md's frontend example still lacks `include`), now filed as a follow-up. No UI-facing change in this fix commit (pure test-config + task-board bookkeeping), so no fresh browser walkthrough was warranted this round — the prior review's lightweight Playwright pass over the three placeholder routes already covers the only UI surface that exists, and nothing about it changed here. The new `decisions` entry recording task-worker's fix rationale is a genuine decision record (what was tried, why, and how it was verified), matching CLAUDE.md's decision-memory standard. No blocking findings remain; moving to done.

pr_decision.notes: Independently re-ran everything rather than trusting the review. Backend: pytest --cov=app matches exactly (472 passed, 99.84% coverage). Frontend: npm ci, then npm run test:coverage/lint/format:check/build/build-storybook all pass (2 test files, 5 tests, 100% on all four coverage dimensions; lcov.info confirms App.tsx + 3 pages + theme.ts are the 5 instrumented files, test files excluded by vitest's default, main.tsx excluded explicitly). Reproduced the empirical coverage-fix test myself from scratch: added src/scratch-untested-verify.ts with an untested if/else branch, reran test:coverage — dropped to 62.5% lines/statements, 0% branches, exit 1 with explicit threshold-failure errors; deleted it and reran — back to a clean 100% exit 0, git status clean. Skimmed the full diff (all 32 changed files): vite.config.ts's include/exclude, tsconfig strict settings, eslint/prettier config, App.tsx route table + test, theme.ts semantic palette + test, main.tsx QueryClient defaults, MSW test harness, Storybook config, and task-board bookkeeping (index.json path/state mirrors, frontend-scaffold-followups.json correctly tracks both non-blocking findings: the unloaded Inter font and Testing.md's doc snippet missing `include`). No new issues found; the accept holds.
